title: MSL/RAD Dose-Rate Reanalysis: Code and Data (msl_2026)
description:
Code and derived data for a 13.5-year (SOL 00001–04843) reanalysis of Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) Curiosity rover RAD dose-rate data, supporting the manuscript "Hysteresis in the Solar-Cycle Modulation of Martian Surface Radiation: 13.5 Years of MSL/RAD Observations Across a Full Cycle Reversal" (Amaral, Abreu dos Anjos, Santos Donato & Bastos Eller; submitted to Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets).

The pipeline extracts detector B and E dose-rate values directly from NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) Reduced Data Records via targeted HTTP range requests (byte-offset extraction from PDS3 detached labels and fixed-length PDS4 tables), avoiding full-file downloads of the ~65 MB RDR files. Real atmospheric pressure is extracted the same way from the Rover Environmental Monitoring Station (REMS) MODRDR product.

Analysis steps included:

  • Robust (rolling-median/MAD) outlier screening for Solar Particle Events
  • Classical additive seasonal decomposition (trend/seasonal/residual) on a real per-sol time axis
  • Continuous wavelet transform (Morlet, pycwt) per ~90-sol window and over the full 13.5-year record
  • Newey–West (HAC) heteroskedasticity- and autocorrelation-consistent regression of dose rate against the smoothed international sunspot number and against the Oulu neutron monitor count rate
  • Lag-scan and phase-split (solar cycle 24 vs. 25) hysteresis test against the neutron-monitor proxy
  • Lomb-Scargle periodogram as a third, independent test for an annual periodicity
  • Conversion of measured dose rate to human mission dose equivalent, cross-validated against Hassler et al. (2014)

Contents: extraction libraries (rad_extract_lib.py, rems_extract_lib.py), 12 numbered analysis scripts, and the derived summary datasets (CSV) each script produces. The full project, including the manuscript and figures, is maintained at github.com/cesarrlamaral/msl_2026.
